overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for debating two bills, a common step known as a "rule" that the House approves before taking up major legislation. The first bill, H.R. 471, would speed up environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act (the law requiring federal agencies to study environmental effects of their projects) for forest management work on national forest, Bureau of Land Management, and Tribal lands to reduce wildfire risk. That bill gets one hour of general debate and only the amendments listed in the Rules Committee's report. The second bill, S. 5, would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain immigrants who are in the country illegally and have been charged with theft; it gets one hour of debate with no amendments allowed. Procedural objections against both bills are waived. The House adopted the resolution on January 22, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule lets the House move quickly to vote on wildfire prevention and public safety bills after an orderly, time-limited debate.
against: Critics say the rule limits debate, blocks most amendments, and waives procedural objections, giving members little chance to change either bill.
